supporting_observations.claim: From 13:40:50 through 14:10:29 UTC, WS-TWEBER-01 made repeated HTTPS tunnel connections through the proxy to update.medledger.com, at roughly five-minute intervals. The proxy records show six connections in this period.

The connections are associated with C:\Program Files\MediLedger\medledgerupd.exe, which initiated proxy-bound connections at the same times; this matches the inventory’s description of the approved MediLedger updater checking update.medledger.com about every five minutes.

The updater process was launched by a PowerShell process running as tom.weber shortly before the first observed connection. The PowerShell command line in the available record shows only the executable path, so the invocation itself is not established.
The updater and its parent PowerShell process both exited shortly after the last observed connection.

known_telemetry_limitations: DC-PIN-01 winsec collection was unavailable from 13:20 to 14:00 UTC due to a log collection outage. This limits corroboration from that sensor during part of the review window.
The available records do not show the PowerShell command or script that launched the updater.
claims_not_established: Whether the PowerShell launch of the approved updater was authorized or expected.
Whether the updater binary was genuine and unmodified; the provided records contain no hash or signature-validation evidence for it.
Whether the alert’s reported periodic activity began at 13:30 UTC: the provided proxy records show the repeated MediLedger connections beginning at 13:40:50 UTC.
additional_evidence_needed: PowerShell script-block, module, or process-command-line telemetry for tom.weber’s PowerShell process around 13:40:48 UTC.
A hash and signature validation for the MediLedger updater, plus its application logs or configuration confirming the observed checks.
Change or user activity records that can establish whether the updater was intentionally launched at that time.
unrelated_findings: WS-TWEBER-01’s Edge browser connected to docs.google.com; the environment inventory says no other file-sharing or cloud-storage services are approved. Treat this as a separate finding, not evidence deciding the alerted MediLedger connections. (T096-00176, T096-00177, T096-00178, T096-00179)

Cisco AnyConnect UI and Palo Alto GlobalProtect UI processes ran on WS-TWEBER-01, despite the inventory stating there is no VPN. The records establish process execution, not a VPN connection. Track separately from this alert. (T096-00143, T096-00144, T096-00145, T096-00274, T096-00275, T096-00276)
